Suppression needs a live baseline showing this envelope routinely carrying events to remove, and it does not have one: C-7d is `window_live: false` with a null payload (no information), C-21d (2026-07-04, a full hour, live) also returned row_count 0, and C-14d (2026-07-11, live) returned a single row — accepted 6, failed 0, svc.config-mgmt from 172.18.0.14 with first_seen == last_seen == 09:47:08.297Z, one scheduled burst in an hour. A live one-hour control that is itself empty means an empty ten-minute observed window is ordinary quiet, which is exactly the measurement's `delta_kind: absent` reading. The projection therefore promotes routine silence into a detection.
rows.evidence: The single query (elastic.sshd-auth-history, 10-minute window 09:35–09:45Z on 2026-07-25) returned row_count 0 with an empty values list, so no source.ip/user.name group was surfaced at all. Of the three controls, C-7d (2026-07-18) has window_live false and payload null, so it carries no information; the two live controls disagree — C-21d (2026-07-04, one hour) also returned row_count 0, while C-14d (2026-07-11, one hour) returned exactly one row (accepted 6, failed 0, user.name svc.config-mgmt, source.ip 172.18.0.14) whose first_seen and last_seen are the same instant 09:47:08.297Z, i.e. a single scheduled burst. Since a live one-hour control already returns zero rows, an empty ten-minute observed window is within routine behaviour rather than a stream going dark, so this is not `suppressed`; and with zero observed rows there is nothing that could be distinguishable in accepted, failed, source.ip or user.name.

Two live controls return a populated baseline for the same host.name == "dev-ws-1": C-14d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 444, elastic_agent.metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 12, elastic_agent.filebeat 6, system.syslog 6 — and C-21d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 528, metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 14, system.syslog 6, filebeat 4. rows.rationale: The lead's single query `cmdb.host-trust-edges` returned only `_note: "state lookup; not an event stream"` and the echoed `params: {host: dev-ws-1}` — no role, criticality, owner, or trust-edge rows, and no timestamped columns. The baseline is `[]` by construction because a CMDB lookup carries no `@timestamp` bounds to shift, which `state_and_lookup_systems` designates `state-only` rather than a dead or missing window, matching the measurement. With no event rows in `observed` and no baseline-diff semantics available, there is no delta for the story's agent-stop on dev-ws-1 to have produced in this envelope. The empty projection therefore asserts nothing false and omits nothing the telemetry carries; had the oracle invented a concrete role/owner/criticality record here it would have been fabrication.
rows.evidence: The lead has a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with params `{host: dev-ws-1}`, and its observed payload carries only `_note: "state lookup; not an event stream"` plus the echoed params — no event rows, no timestamped columns. The baseline is an empty list because a CMDB lookup carries no `@timestamp` bounds to shift, so no control window exists by construction. Per `state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries return an entity record rather than an event stream and have no baseline-diff semantics. This is `state-only`, not a missing or dead-window measurement, and with only one decidable query there is no cross-query disagreement to record.
